messages:
Incident Bot: PagerDuty alert triggered -> PD-9427. Service: inference-hotpath.p99_latency_ms > 1500ms (5m window) region=us-west

PagerDuty: SEV: high — initial alert at 23:01 UTC

Sasha: acked PD-9427. i'm taking first pass. quick heads-up: p99 spiking to ~2.1s, p95 ~820ms. timeouts observed on sync text-gen. creating incident INC-2024-07-23-7

Kevin: joining now, what does monitoring show?

Sasha: looks like a high tail traffic burst. GPU pool inference-gpu-pool at 96% util, queue depth growing. KV cache miss% climbed to ~40% from baseline 5-8%.

Anya: any single-tenant abnormality? can we isolate?

Sasha: yes — large spike from tenant `Brightline` (enterprise). lots of long completions >1200 tokens.

Kevin: ok. quick mitigation proposal: 1) reduce max_batch_size on hotpath route, 2) route long requests to cheaper fallback model, 3) manual scale + warm nodes.

Sasha: applying batch cap now. sending config change:
```
PUT /routes/hotpath/config
{"max_batch_size":12, "batch_latency_slo_ms":70}
```

Incident Bot: route config update deployed (rev r1102)

Kevin: kicking manual scale:
```bash
rctl scale pool inference-gpu-pool --add 3
# expected join time ~90-120s
```

Kevin: concurrently warming compact fallback on pool nodes to avoid cold starts.

Dave: priming KV cache for top prefixes. running primer job to pre-populate top 200 prefixes to edge caches.

Dave: running:
```bash
./tools/kv_primer --top=200 --dest=edge
```

CS Team: notified Brightline CS contact; they reported timeouts from ~23:00-23:06 UTC. asking for ETA and mitigation notes.

Sasha: routing override applied for Brightline -> redwood-compact-v1-quant on fallback-gpu-pool.
```bash
rctl route override --tenant Brightline --model redwood-compact-v1-quant --pool fallback-gpu-pool
```

PagerDuty: note added to PD-9427: routing override for Brightline applied by Sasha

Sasha: p99 trend: 5m p99 down to ~1.45s after batch cap and routing. still above 1.0s target but improving. queue depth trending down.

Kevin: new nodes are healthy; pool util now ~80%. starting gradual shift of small requests back to primary.

Dave: KV miss-rate now ~10% after priming. much better.

Anya: quick impact estimate from CS: Brightline saw majority of errors, 6 other customers saw intermittent increased latency with retries mostly succeeding. no customer data loss.

Sasha: incident status: mitigations applied (batch cap, KV priming, scaling, routing override). recommended next steps: 1) track for 20-30m, 2) follow-up postmortem, 3) autoscaler tuning. handing to Anya for watch handoff.

Anya: taking over watch. summary for handoff:
- incident: INC-2024-07-23-7 (PD-9427)
- suspected cause: sudden long-sequence burst from Brightline causing prefix churn and queue growth -> high p99
- mitigations: reduced max_batch_size, primed KV cache, added nodes, warmed fallback, routed Brightline to fallback pool
- current status: 5m p99 ~930ms, KV miss-rate ~8%, queue stable
- customer impact: Brightline experienced timeouts; 6 others saw transient latency spikes
- owners: Kevin -> autoscaler tuning + node warmers; Dave -> integrate KV primer into runtime deploy; Sasha -> timeline + logs into INF postmortem ticket

Anya: i'll monitor and coordinate customer comms. will post updates every 10 minutes until clear.

Sasha: leaving channel, ping if anything spikes again. :thumbsup:

Incident Bot: PD-9427 acknowledged and marked under investigation -> mitigations in progress

PagerDuty: PD-9427 escalated to on-call manager initially; escalation closed after manual mitigation applied

Anya: 23:18 UTC update: p99 steady ~880ms for last 10m, KV miss-rate stable ~7%, queue normal. marking as monitored. drafting ops note and cs summary.

Anya: filing follow-ups in Jira: INF-4601 (postmortem), INF-4602 (autoscaler response improvements), INF-4603 (kv-primer rollout)

Sasha: thanks all. closing active pager. will attach logs and timeline to INF-4601.

Incident Bot: PD-9427 resolved (alert cleared) at 23:22 UTC

Anya: final handoff: CS to send Brightline brief explaining cause and mitigations, offer logs if requested. Dave will open PR for prefix-churn detector alert.

Dave: PR for prefix churn detector in draft, will tag Kevin for review.

Kevin: will also add a small quickscale policy for sustained queue growth to reduce manual ops.

Anya: thanks team. monitoring until 23:52 UTC then handing to next oncall.

Sasha: great work everyone.
